title: Part 1
text: Imagine a disease that makes people tremble, lose their balance, and burst into laughter they cannot control. It was real, and it appeared in a remote corner of Papua New Guinea.

title: Part 2
text: In the 1950s, doctors reached the eastern highlands, where the Fore people lived. There, a mysterious illness was killing many of them. The Fore called it kuru, a word that means shaking.
nxt: Outsiders gave it a darker name: the laughing death.

title: Part 3
text: It began with clumsiness. A person would stumble on a path they had walked a thousand times.
nxt: Then came tremors, slurred speech, and sudden fits of laughter that had nothing to do with joy.

title: Part 4
text: Doctors were stumped. There was no fever. There was no sign of bacteria. It did not behave like malaria or influenza. And the pattern was strange.
nxt: Kuru struck women and children far more often than adult men.

title: Part 5
text: The clue was hidden in a funeral custom. Among the Fore, relatives of the dead sometimes practiced mortuary cannibalism.
nxt: Anthropologists who studied the custom describe it as an act of mourning and respect, a way to keep a loved one inside the family.

title: Part 6
text: According to those accounts, the body was shared by custom. Men often received the muscle.
nxt: Women and children were more likely to handle and eat other tissues, including the brain. And the brain was where the danger was concentrated.

title: Part 7
text: In the 1950s, the physician Carleton Gajdusek and the medical officer Vincent Zigas began to study the disease together.
nxt: Years later, brain tissue from kuru victims was injected into chimpanzees. After a long wait, the animals developed the same illness. Kuru was infectious.

title: Part 8
text: Think about how cruel that is. A ritual created out of love became the path by which a deadly disease moved from one person to the next. Nobody in the valley could have known.
nxt: The germ was invisible, and the illness might not appear for many years.

title: Part 9
text: That is how a sacred act of love became a toxic transmission line. But the real mystery was only beginning.
nxt: What kind of infection could hide in the brain for decades, ignore every known treatment, and leave no trace of a germ?
